items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: They had this colored act come to Long Branch to the Main Street theatre, named J. Rosamond Johnson and Company. J. Rosamond Johnson was a hell of a piano player.

ctx.x: So she say, 'You're through'. So she gave me a little old dollar, got a dollar for walking around 18 holes and that was terrible. The bag weighed a ton, so I left the bag, --she anyway she want-- get it and walked off. So in the meantime, that went on -- I didn't have no job. I lost that job completely.

So in the meantime at Long Branch they used to have the Keith vaudeville acts, come to the theatre for a week. They had a colored act there -- when you were on Keith's Circuit, that was the top of the heap, like the Palace was heaven, the Palace Theatre in New York, but Keith's circuit all they acts, was the fine combed, the best in the world. They had this colored act come to Long Branch to the Main Street theatre, named J. Rosamond Johnson and Company. J. Rosamond Johnson was a hell of a piano player. The…

I went to see them, so this guy, this drummer he fascinated me, oh, he was so sharp, man. He sang, he danced and he played those drums just so nonchalant, effortless, just like falling off a log. I looked at this guy and I had to go back and see him again. They were there for a week.
